title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 752-754 of the 'suite à la Longue Marche'). The previous page has the following data. Pi_0 is a discrete group (in the Longue Marche setting, presumably a Teichmüller/surface-type group; possibly a finitely generated group with unipotent behaviour). Pi_Q is a Q-algebraic envelope of Pi_0 (the 'Env' of §50). G_0 (gothic G) is a larger discrete group containing Pi_0, with algebraic envelope G_Q. M is a profinite group of Galois type that receives G_0, together with a Q-group M_Q containing G_Q and a character chi_M : M_Q -> G_m,Q, which plays the role of the cyclotomic character. 'Tori' T_0 are free abelian groups, likely multitwist subgroups; there is a finite set of conjugacy classes of homomorphisms k_i : T_0 -> Pi_0, which extend to K_i : G_a ⊗ T_0 -> Pi_Q. Grothendieck then assumes M_Q comes from an affine flat finite-type Z-group scheme M with M -> M(Ẑ) (45).

This page:
(i) Integral models. Let Pi and G be the schematic closures of Pi_Q and G_Q in M. They are flat closed subgroup schemes over Z, giving a chain Pi ⊂ G ⊂ M of Z-group schemes (46). The page names three quotients: 𝒯 = G/Pi, Gamma = M/G, N = M/Pi. Representability of these quotients is waved through 'by Raynaud'. Over a Dedekind base of dimension 1 this is essentially the Raynaud–Anantharaman theory: quotients of flat affine finite-type group schemes by flat closed normal subgroups are representable.
(ii) Integral points (47). Pi_0 and G_0 sit in Pi_Q(Q) and G_Q(Q). Their images in M(Ẑ) lie in M(Q) ∩ M(Ẑ) = M(Z), using flatness and affineness. A Z-point of M whose generic fibre lies in Pi_Q is a Z-point of the closure Pi. This gives the commutative diagram Pi_0 ↪ G_0 -> M over Pi(Z) ↪ G(Z) ↪ M(Ẑ).
(iii) The character. Grothendieck assumes chi_M extends to chi : M -> G_m,Z (48). Since chi is trivial on G_Q, it is trivial on the closure G (G is flat and G_m is separated), so it factors through Gamma = M/G (49). On Ẑ-points this recovers a cyclotomic-type character M -> Ẑ^*.

Purpose (as the next page shows): to find a smooth 'model' M over Z of the algebraic envelope of a Galois-type action. The model should be compatible with the profinite group and with the cyclotomic character, and Grothendieck asks for an existence (even uniqueness) theorem. He then studies how the tori homomorphisms K_i and their centralisers extend integrally.
errors: The factorisation of chi_M through Gamma (49) silently requires chi_M to be trivial on G_Q. This is presumably part of the setup (G_0 lies in the kernel of the cyclotomic-type character) but is not stated on this page.

Representability 'jamais de pb par Raynaud' is roughly right but slightly glib. The relevant results over a Dedekind base are Raynaud's quotient theory (1967) and its completion by Anantharaman (1973). Over general bases, quotients of flat group schemes are only algebraic spaces. Over Z with flat closed normal subgroups the claim is fine.
Notation clash: the quotient G/Pi is denoted by a script T, while T_0 and T_i also denote the 'tori'.
The bottom row writes G(Z) ↪ M(Ẑ) as if direct. It really factors through M(Z) ⊂ M(Ẑ), with injectivity coming from flatness of M.

ideas.what: Integral models of algebraic envelopes of discrete groups, obtained as schematic closures inside a chosen Z-model of an ambient group.
ideas.modern_name: Schematic closure / integral models of linear algebraic groups (Bruhat–Tits style integral structures; integral structures on unipotent/relative completions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard EGA IV technique; integral structures on completions studied later by Deligne (1989), Hain–Matsumoto and others
ideas.where_published: Schematic closure in EGA IV; the specific application here is unpublished

ideas.what: Representability of quotients of flat group schemes over Z.
ideas.modern_name: Quotients of flat group schemes over a Dedekind base
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 for quotients over fields and in some relative cases

ideas.what: A Galois-type profinite group M mapped to the Ẑ-points of a Z-group scheme M, with a character M -> G_m,Z extending the cyclotomic character and factoring through the 'arithmetic' quotient Gamma = M/G.
ideas.modern_name: Relative / weighted completion of an arithmetic fundamental group relative to the cyclotomic character, with an integral structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, ~2003); Deligne (1989) for integral/motivic structure of unipotent pi_1

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a three-step filtration Pi ⊂ G ⊂ M of Z-group schemes. It models (geometric fundamental group) ⊂ (arithmetic discrete group envelope) ⊂ (Galois-type group), with the cyclotomic character factoring through the top quotient. This anticipates relative/weighted completions of arithmetic fundamental and mapping-class groups (Hain–Matsumoto) but asks for an integral (smooth over Z) model, which the later literature mostly treats only over Q or Q_l.
missed.quote: les adhérences schématiques dans M de Pi_Q, G_Q, d'où un diagramme de schémas en groupes sur Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of relative completions compatible with the profinite Galois action are not standard. The question of existence and uniqueness of a smooth Z-model (posed on the next page) remains a natural open-ended problem.

missed.claim: The existence/uniqueness of the Z-model M with M -> M(Ẑ) and chi extending to G_m,Z is assumed here ('il me semble qu'on peut trouver un tel M') and only posed as a desideratum on the next page.
missed.quote: On suppose bien sûr que l'homomorphisme chi_M : M_Q -> G_m Q se prolonge en chi_M : M -> G_m Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, unresolved formulation of integrality for algebraic envelopes of Galois actions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is routine scheme-theoretic bookkeeping: schematic closures, Raynaud-type quotients and extension of a character. Its interest lies in the setting, an integral-over-Z version of a relative completion with cyclotomic character from the late 1980s/1990s, which partially anticipates weighted completion. The mathematics on the page is not new, and the setup's identification is somewhat uncertain.
transcription_corrections: The label over Pi ⊂ G in (46) is a script T (𝒯), distinct from the tori T_0.
The inserted text after the deletion reads approximately 'On a des factorisations', replacing a struck phrase (roughly 'supposé d'un sous-gr...').
In 'On suppose bien sûr que', the struck word is roughly 'hypothétique'.
In (47) the right vertical arrow is M -> M(Ẑ) from (45). The bottom row is Pi(Z) ↪ G(Z) ↪ M(Ẑ).
